title: The Translational Path of Mitochondrial Transplantation for Pulmonary Fibrosis
content: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a chronic and progressive fibrotic lung disease associated with mitochondrial dysfunction. Mitochondrial transplantation (MTx) has recently emerged as a promising regenerative medicine strategy for diseases associated with mitochondrial dysfunction. Growing evidence supports the therapeutic potential of MTx in pulmonary fibrosis. Preclinical studies have demonstrated that the delivery of healthy mitochondria can improve mitochondrial function, reduce fibrotic responses, and restore cellular homeostasis in experimental models of lung fibrosis. However, the available evidence is largely limited to in vitro and animal studies, each of which captures only select features of IPF and fails to fully reproduce the complexity of human disease. Consequently, the translation of these promising findings into clinical therapies remains challenging. To better understand the opportunities and limitations of MTx in IPF, this paper examines the experimental platforms currently used in the field. The physiological relevance, translational value, and ability to bridge the gap between mechanistic discovery and clinical application are given. The selection of appropriate experimental models is critical for advancing the field. Each platform offers distinct advantages and limitations. Combining complementary platforms may provide the most effective strategy for evaluating mitochondrial-based therapies and accelerating clinical translation.
